column1: # Every action this project can bind a key to -- and so every action a screen
# edge of ours can run, which is the same list on purpose.
# One list for everything that needs it. shortcuts.sh reads it for what it
# accepts and what it shows, edges.sh for what an edge may name, doctor for
# what to look for; bin/windowsd/brand.py.in has it rendered in, to register each
# one with kglobalaccel and to run it. Before this there were three copies and
# a fourth that held eight of the fourteen.
# The id, a tab, the name System Settings shows in its shortcut list -- a
# sentence a person recognises, not the id -- a tab, and the arguments to the
# CLI that runs it, split on spaces. In the order `shortcuts status` lists them.
